root_cause.text: The NVMe host driver's `nvme_alloc_admin_tag_set` function leaks the admin queue resource because it overwrites the `ctrl->admin_q` pointer without first releasing the reference to the existing queue via `blk_put_queue()` during a controller reset.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (ctrl->admin_q) blk_put_queue(ctrl->admin_q);` before the assignment `ctrl->admin_q = blk_mq_alloc_queue(...)` in `drivers/nvme/host/core.c`, explicitly handling the cleanup of the previously existing queue referenced in the CVE description.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fixes a reference leak by releasing the previous admin queue before allocating a new one during tag set initialization.
intent_record.what: Inserted a conditional block to check if ctrl->admin_q exists and call blk_put_queue() on it before assigning a new queue.
intent_record.how: Ensures the reference count of any pre-existing admin queue is decremented, preventing resource leaks during controller reinitialization or reset scenarios.

relevance_review.reason: The group's intent explicitly describes fixing the reference leak of the admin queue by releasing the previous queue before allocation, which directly addresses the root cause of the resource leak in nvme_alloc_admin_tag_set.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement overwrites the ctrl->admin_q pointer without first calling blk_put_queue() to release the reference to the existing queue. During controller reset, when nvme_alloc_admin_tag_set is called and fails or needs to reinitialize, the old admin queue reference is leaked because the pointer is simply set to NULL without proper cleanup.
